approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES prior on unlabeled molecules and selects its checkpoint by the number of valid, connected, distinct ancestral molecules under a fixed sampling probe, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable flow policy and keeps that selected prior frozen. Accepted molecular trajectories train the policy through trajectory balance and prior regularization. The search alternates one neural batch with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a scored breeding population and supply a protected first descendant; crossover and seven atom/bond mutation families build temporary offspring pools, and an accepted-score fingerprint posterior selects the remaining evaluations. Accepted graph discoveries can then breed again and train the neural policy. The graph atom-replacement step chooses an atom uniformly and substitutes an element allowed by its current bond valence; a fully bonded carbonyl carbon consequently has no replacement option.
approach.novelty: At those otherwise unsuccessful carbonyl-carbon replacement sites, add one direct reversal of a qualifying secondary amide: A-C(=O)-NH-B becomes A-NH-C(=O)-B while both attached fragments and the molecular formula remain intact. This makes the opposite arrangement of the amide donor and carbonyl acceptor available without passing through independent destructive substitutions. The same-parent graph children moved nitrogen within aromatic rings or matched crossover attachment contexts; neither supplied this amide-orientation move. The new move retains the inherited selection of atoms and operators and adds no protection gate over ordinary replacements.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 has a complete three-seed macro mean of 0.5501977216134929 and population SD 0.02173839408580094. Its per-seed summary.json and run.log all report successful completion, and its graph logs join to 2850 accepted graph emissions, of which 452 strictly beat their best actual generating parent (157, 145 and 150 across the supplied replicas). Its molecular assessment reports abundant amides and carbonyl-containing frameworks but incomplete exploration of useful functional-group arrangements. Source inspection identifies a specific missing move: replace_atom cannot change a neutral secondary-amide carbonyl carbon because its bond valence is four, leaving only carbon in the element menu, which is then removed as the current element. Neither that single substitution nor another single inherited mutation reverses the intact A-C(=O)-NH-B relationship. A read-only structural census of all 4500 Parent accepted records finds 625 records with 655 qualifying sites under the proposed acyclic, neutral, carbon-substituted secondary-amide predicate that excludes imide nitrogens; direct diagnostic reversal gives 655 valid formula-preserving nonidentity products, counted separately within each record. Site counts are 192, 238 and 225 in the supplied replicas. These products carry no scores and the counts do not establish global novelty. There are also 3675 Parent graph attempts without successful crossover whose first accepted source carries such a site; those are source opportunities, not observed carbonyl-site selections. Sibling n-32ac3137615b establishes that a direct conserved-composition positional channel can reach evaluation, but its total parent-beating yield falls from 452 to 449 despite higher endpoints. Cross-lineage n-9bee44b1c9c3 preserves carbonyl atoms while still changing adjacent functional-group classes and loses mean score. Together these observations motivate adding a complete amide-orientation alternative at a currently empty local action, without assuming that carbonyl retention or local formula preservation causes better scores.
hypothesis: Rescue otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon replace_atom choices with a direct orientation reversal of an acyclic carbon-substituted secondary amide, preserving its molecular formula and both attached fragments.

finding_summary.headline: Amide reversals reach evaluation without a local score gain, despite higher endpoints
finding_summary.insights: The experiment establishes a working, evaluated amide-orientation channel, and rules out failure to construct the move as the explanation for its weak measured utility. It does not support the proposed local score benefit. Exposure narrows sharply after construction: 46 admitted reversals remained unevaluated, including every crossover-derived reversal. Two direct pairs cannot establish which amide environments might benefit more broadly. The higher endpoints also occur amid changed pool competition, random-number consumption and later search feedback; they cannot be attributed to a favorable amide reversal when neither observed direct pair wins. The molecular assessment reinforces the narrower chemical interpretation: familiar medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive linkages, small-ring cumulenes and unspecified configurations. Conserving one amide and its attached fragments does not resolve those broader quality gaps. A useful next causal question is whether valid local alternatives fail mainly through limited evaluation exposure or through context-dependent score neutrality; the present panel leaves that distinction open. The ancestry audit also shows why crossover parent labels must be followed through subsequent deletions before interpreting parent-relative scores.
finding_summary.results: Across all three seeds and five objectives, 51 selected secondary-amide sites produced 51 valid, distinct-from-source reversals with the registered formula, fragment and ring preservation. That is 0.420% of 12,153 atom-replacement attempts. Thirty-six were sole mutations of accepted parents and 15 followed crossover. Forty-eight products entered temporary pools; only two were evaluated, both as sole reversals. The zaleplon pair tied at 0.273668, while the deco_hop pair fell from 0.594245 to 0.580622. There were no direct wins, one tie and one loss, with mean difference −0.006811. Overall graph parent-beating yield fell from the logged Parent reference of 452/2,850 (15.86%) to 389/2,850 (13.65%). Correcting an inherited crossover attribution error raises the Parent count to 453 and leaves the Child count unchanged. All batches filled and all 150 fresh-policy handoffs had real fresh-parent contribution. Meanwhile, mean endpoint score rose from 0.550198 to 0.570186; the paired seed changes were +0.042122, +0.022690 and −0.004846, with the largest mean task gain in deco_hop.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom links, small-ring cumulenes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The complete supplied panel covers all five tasks and seeds 0, 1 and 2: each task has 900 accepted trajectory records, including 870 optimizer proposals. No task lacks trajectories. Both this node and Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 were read across that panel. The output contains recognizable aryl ethers, nitriles, benzimidazoles, quinazolines, saturated amines, lactams, sulfonamides and indoles, together with unusually connected sulfur/oxygen groups and extensively rearranged unsaturated rings. Digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9644 to 0.9954 and aromatic-marker rates from 0.7103 to 0.9747; these are string-level presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived rings. Ring chemistry and aromatic chemistry are abundant. The complete output spans many frameworks, although each seed's upper tail often concentrates on a particular family. Practical-looking building blocks coexist with questionable assembled structures, so broad diversity does not establish broadly plausible synthesis. Every digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception of the optimizer trajectories finds molecules with unspecified atom stereocentres in counts of 351, 251, 451, 316 and 378 in the brief's task order, with no assigned atom centres; absence of stereo annotation therefore does not mean the output is achiral. Structural counts below are derived from the supplied molecular records, and all scores are existing trajectory scores. The digest's final excerpts are seed-2 samples, not a summary of every seed's final state.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 structure is a medium-sized nitrile attached to an unsaturated seven-membered oxygen ring, with phenyl, aryl ether, pyridyl and aminomethyl functionality. RDKit reads 24 heavy atoms and three rings, two aromatic. Its relatives interchange ether, sulfur, O-S, S-S and peroxide linkages while retaining much of that arrangement. Seed 1 instead produces N-alkoxycarbonyl or N-acyl benzimidazole-like cores bearing a halogenated anilinomethyl substituent, with an N-O-containing ring-expanded relative also near the top. Seed 0 follows phenolic hydroxycyclobutene/imine structures joined to an expanded nitrogen-containing ring. Thus the pooled leaders do not describe the whole seed panel. The optimizer's median heavy-atom count is 25 in both this node and the Parent. The Parent's seed-0 leaders were fused aza-ring structures with unusual O/N/S attachments; its other seeds included aryl carboxamides and nitrile-containing unsaturated rings. The current molecules retain moderate molecular scale and aromatic/polar combinations while changing their assembly. The ether/nitrile and halogenated heterocycle families contain recognizable synthetic fragments, but the unusual heteroatom bonds and ring arrangements make feasibility uneven.
liabilities: Peroxide, O-S, S-S and N-O connectivity occurs among favorable examples. Those bonds change the chemical class and possible stability of the linker or ring; their accepted scores do not establish interchangeable synthetic behavior.
The hydroxycyclobutene/imine and expanded aza-ring output, and the fused cumulated-double-bond example, raise geometry and chemical-persistence questions beyond simple SMILES validity.
RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 351 of 870 optimizer proposals and assigned centres in none. The leading seven-membered oxygen-ring example itself has an unspecified centre.
missing_features: A more complete series of chemically credible alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic, polar and linker relationships is not demonstrated. The distinct favorable nitrile/ether and N-acyl heterocycle families do not reveal one uniquely missing required group.
Defined configurations are absent at the substituted oxygen-ring centre and in other saturated ring variants. The observed scores do not identify a preferred configuration.
Controlled compact core and linker changes remain incompletely represented: the late duplicated nitrile ring and fused cumulene do not retain the leading score despite retaining recognizable pieces.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryloxy nitrile leader scores 0.48839749189747395, the related O-S linker 0.47582689034774595, and the sulfur linker 0.46457806514522626. The peroxide-linked relative still scores 0.4526205390674507. The N-alkoxycarbonyl benzimidazole and its N-O ring-expanded relative each score 0.4588069837338257 despite lacking the leading family's nitrile. These observations associate higher scores with particular medium-sized connected aromatic/polar arrangements; they do not make nitrile or an unusual heteroatom linkage a universal requirement. Methane, hydroxylamine and the much larger polyol/amide assembly have scores of 0.0, and an overgrown amino/amidine-rich assembly scores 7.335113523278365e-48. A late structure duplicating the unsaturated nitrile-containing ring scores 0.26198042135705957, while a fused cumulated-double-bond variant scores 0.18422963024144726. The pooled median is 0.152555. Relative to the Parent, the sampled maximum decreases in seed 0 from 0.49151859442707624 to 0.4412371986661207, and increases in seeds 1 and 2 from 0.4163503402962837 and 0.46457806514522626 to 0.4588069837338257 and 0.48839749189747395. The chemistry changes differ by seed; these comparisons do not isolate the cause of those score changes.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-0 family consists of anilinoquinazolines with fluorine/chlorine substitution, methoxy or amino groups, and oxygen-linked side chains. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-membered rings. Its aminomethoxy substituent contains an N-Cl bond; many nearby leaders instead carry an aryl peroxide, and some add an O-Cl group. A favorable ether-linked relative lacks the peroxide and N-Cl linkage. Seed 1 explores quinazoline/carbonyl arrangements with nitrile-bearing thiophenes, acylated amines and piperazinones, sometimes in very large linked assemblies. Seed 2 samples linked pyrimidine, benzimidazole and pyridyl regions with nitrogen-rich connecting rings and N-N attachments. The median size is 33 heavy atoms, compared with 36 for the Parent, with a median of four rings in both. Parent seed 0 favored a different sulfonamide/aza-ring family; Parent seed 1 already had linked quinazoline/piperazinone chemistry, and Parent seed 2 had aminoalkyl aza-aromatic structures. Conventional heteroaromatic and amide components are readily recognizable, but the high-ranking peripheral chemistry is not consistently plausible as a stable finished compound.
liabilities: The highest-scoring molecule contains N-Cl, several near-leading molecules contain O-O, and one contains O-Cl. Carbon-bound chlorine elsewhere in these molecules is a different chemical environment and should not be conflated with those heteroatom-halogen bonds.

Read-only graph perception finds O-O bonds in 130 optimizer proposals, compared with 135 in the Parent. The concern persists across a substantial sampled family and is not confined to a single isolated low-score example.
Expanded linked assemblies and unusual nitrogen-rich rings complicate geometry and synthesis. RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 251 optimizer proposals, with none assigned.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives around the favorable aza-aromatic attachment pattern are only partly demonstrated. An ether-linked high example exists, so the missing capability is consistent coverage of credible alternatives, not the mere ability to emit an ether.
Useful core/attachment diversity is uneven across seeds: the strong anilinoquinazoline family does not establish a similarly successful alternative core in the seed-2 nitrogen-rich neighborhood.

Specified stereochemistry is absent for substituted alkyl side chains and more complex saturated variants. Nothing in the displayed scores identifies the preferred configuration or a uniquely absent functional group.

A related compound with ether side chains and no peroxide or N-Cl bond scores 0.9310417418501142. Thus the upper values tolerate concerning linkages, but do not establish that those linkages are needed. The styryl/sulfone/hydroxamate low example scores 0.2712455185234365; a separate imide/amine/sulfone assembly scores 0.2829523943069481. Ring and heteroatom abundance alone do not reproduce the favorable connected aza-aromatic arrangement. Late seed-2 linked nitrogen heterocycles score 0.6118381518328103 and 0.6065763384005287, and the pooled median is 0.581568. The seed-0 maximum changes from the Parent's 0.6039553752535497 to 0.9389438334932467 with a different leading family. The seed-1 maximum changes from 0.8301591128254581 to 0.8493261266320371 within broader quinazoline/carbonyl chemistry; seed 2 remains close, from 0.6153794851273843 to 0.6138259512405145. These are associations across whole trajectories, not evidence for a specific binding interaction or for a reactive group's utility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are arylpiperazines with flexible alkyl linkers to another aromatic group or an N-aryl five-membered heterocycle. The brominated/chlorinated leader has 32 heavy atoms and four rings, three aromatic, and a six-carbon linker to piperazine. A simpler high example is a fluorophenylpiperazine linked through five carbons to phenyl. Seed 0 instead explores aryl-substituted saturated diazepane amines attached to fused aromatic/imine systems, including indole and thiol groups. Seed 1 retains heavily fused or bridged aryl/ether/amine structures. This node's median size is 28 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with the Parent's 30 heavy atoms and four rings. The Parent already emitted the same leading seed-1 and seed-2 families; the main change among those leading structures is in seed 0. Accessible saturated amines and aromatic surfaces are abundant. The digest charged-marker rate of 0.008 does not measure basic-amine coverage: the neutral SMILES of arylpiperazines and other saturated amines can contain protonatable centres. Simple arylpiperazine/linker assemblies look synthetically recognizable, whereas the densely bridged variants require substantially more scrutiny.
liabilities: Long flexible chains, repeated aromatic surfaces and substantial halogen substitution leave physical-property balance unestablished. High accepted scores are not measurements of solubility, selectivity or practical exposure.
Thiol-bearing relatives and extensively fused or bridged structures introduce chemical-persistence and synthetic-geometry questions that the SMILES and scores do not resolve.

RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 451 of 870 optimizer proposals, with none assigned. This primarily concerns the broader substituted and polycyclic output rather than every quoted linear arylpiperazine.
missing_features: No uniquely absent pharmacophore can be inferred from an upper tail already near the observed score limit. Saturated basic-amine candidates and aromatic surfaces are present.

Defined configurations are absent in the fused and bridged amine families, and a controlled series of linker geometries is not established by the displayed leaders. The linear-linker leaders themselves need not contain a tetrahedral stereocentre.
Compact alternatives that retain the favorable aromatic/accessible-amine arrangement without multiplying large arms are incompletely controlled.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl/heteroaryl hexyl-piperazine leader scores 0.9999999657062248, its thiol-substituted relative 0.9999999149875901, and the simpler fluorophenylpiperazine/pentylphenyl molecule 0.9999993790262016. The extra heteroaromatic ring and extensive halogenation are therefore not demonstrated necessities. The Parent already has the same leading seed-2 value and the same seed-1 maximum of 0.9999943278368041; the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.98747470209114 to 0.9999971866054931 with the altered amine/aromatic family. The pooled median is 0.724445. At the low end, an N-acyl/sulfonyl aromatic molecule scores 3.8021829379963674e-05, a nitro acylhydrazone 4.1105044111594925e-05, and a sulfonamide/hydroxamate 5.916130606141068e-05. A piperazine whose nitrogens are tied into thiourea and amide environments scores 0.00015556264858674598. This supports a distinction between accessible amines and electronically deactivated nitrogen, while the different whole structures prevent a causal assignment to basicity alone. Duplicating large aromatic/amine arms produces a late score of only 0.046770493414912545. The observed preference concerns the connected aromatic/amine/linker arrangement, rather than maximizing nitrogen or molecular bulk.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecule is a methylenedioxy-fused benzodiazepinone-like system attached to an aryl sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine. It has 32 heavy atoms and five rings, including a seven-membered imine/lactam ring. Related seed-1 leaders contain bromomethyl or bromoethyl heteroaromatic lactams and chlorinated biphenyl groups joined to the sulfonylpiperazine. Seed 2 favors an indole-containing oxygen ring linked through an ether to a fused nitrogen/dicarbonyl system; late examples replace a ring carbon with oxygen or nitrogen. Seed 0 produces fused aromatic/dicarbonyl systems with sulfur-oxygen ring links. The median size is 32 heavy atoms and four rings in both this node and the Parent. The leading seed-1 and seed-2 structures and scores are retained from the Parent, while seed 0 changes from more sulfonylmorpholine-bearing assemblies to the sulfur/oxygen-linked fused family. Lactam, sulfonamide, piperazine and indole components are familiar medicinal chemistry, but their detailed ring assembly and some late substitutions make synthetic plausibility uneven.
liabilities: Alkyl bromides occur in several favorable relatives, and an O-O bond occurs in a favorable indole-linked oxygen ring. Those changes introduce distinct possible reactivity concerns and cannot be treated as chemically neutral decoration.

O-O single bonds occur in 47 optimizer proposals, compared with 50 in the Parent. The compact leading diazepinone lacks that liability, so the judgment concerns inconsistent quality within the output.
The fused/linked carbonyl systems and acetal-like centres have unresolved configurations. RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 316 optimizer proposals and none assigned.
missing_features: Stable and configurationally specified variations of the indole-linked oxygen-ring family are incompletely demonstrated. The peroxide and O-N replacements do not establish an objective-required group.

Compact core replacements that retain the useful lactam, aromatic and amine relationships remain incompletely covered. The leading diazepinone already shows that the larger brominated biaryl architecture is not universally necessary.
The structures do not identify a uniquely missing target-like scaffold or preferred stereoisomer; stereochemical specification and controlled functional-group placement are the observable gaps.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 structures are compact sulfonyl/sulfinyl nitrogen compounds bearing fluoroacetyl groups and highly unsaturated carbon frameworks. The best molecule has 26 heavy atoms, one five-membered carbon ring and no aromatic ring by RDKit perception. It contains an acyclic allene/polyene segment and a five-membered ring with consecutive cumulated double bonds; the nitrogens are acylated or sulfur-bound rather than ordinary free alkylamines. Aromatic relatives occur in the same high family, including an aniline and a benzyl-substituted sulfonamide-like arrangement. Seed 0 instead favors compact nitrogen-rich fused rings with pyridyl/imine and oxime-ether functionality. Seed 2 samples carbonyl-rich chains with sulfur/nitrogen attachments, acylurea-like units or a carboxylic/carbamic mixed-anhydride linkage, connected through oxygen to unsaturated nitrogen rings. The median size remains 24 heavy atoms, as in the Parent. Parent seed 0 had a different oxygen/nitrogen bicyclic family, Parent seed 1 already had sulfonyl/sulfinyl unsaturated-ring structures, and Parent seed 2 included indole-linked ureas. The current output therefore has polar groups and compact scaffolds, but the high seed-1 family is particularly questionable as isolable finished molecules.
liabilities: The five-membered cyclic cumulene is a strong geometry and persistence concern inferred from its connectivity. Small-ring cumulenes are known to impose substantial geometric strain; this contextual concern is supported by the primary study [Strain estimates for small-ring cyclic allenes and butatrienes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16839152/). No stability or strain value is assigned here to a generated molecule.

The digest cumulated-double-bond rate is 0.1207, corresponding to 105 optimizer strings; the same string-level check finds 4 in the Parent panel. The aromatic-marker rate is 0.7103 despite the ring-closure rate of 0.9644, consistent with extensive nonaromatic unsaturated-ring exploration rather than absent rings.

Sulfenamide-like S-N attachments and mixed-anhydride connectivity in the late carbonyl-rich molecules raise additional chemical-context questions. They are chemically different from ordinary thioethers, amides and carbamates.
RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 378 optimizer proposals and none assigned. The leading sulfinyl structure itself has an unspecified atom stereocentre.

A less-unsaturated ring relative is present, so this is incomplete coverage rather than total absence.

Defined configurations at substituted saturated atoms and sulfinyl centres are absent, and relevant double-bond geometry is not established by the cited strings. The data do not establish a preferred configuration.

The output does not reveal a uniquely absent target pharmacophore. Nitrogen, fluorine, carbonyl and sulfur functionality are already represented; their useful arrangement remains incompletely resolved across the different seed families.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading N-Cl-containing molecule scores 0.9389438334932467, a peroxide-containing relative 0.9361879682516134, and a related ether-containing molecule without those bonds 0.9310417418501142. An indole-linked oxygen-ring member scores 0.2371358719187444 while its peroxide-containing relative remains at 0.23322188283655107. O-S, S-S and mixed-anhydride examples also occur in the cited output. Concerning chemical classes therefore survive in favorable neighborhoods alongside more conventional alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group changes do not consistently retain chemically credible local bonding around otherwise useful molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide context-sensitive edits that retain useful surrounding aromatic and polar relationships while offering coherent amide, ether, amine and sulfur-group alternatives. Distinguish peroxide formation, heteroatom halogenation, sulfenamide formation and mixed-anhydride formation from changes within ordinary functional-group classes. Use the available accepted feedback to compare the actual alternatives; their presence alone does not establish a reason to remove every occurrence of a heteroatom or halogen.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One complete supplied panel contains 105 strings with a cumulated-double-bond marker, versus 4 in its Parent panel. Its leading cited molecule, scoring 0.43965957023019037, has a five-membered cyclic cumulene and no aromatic ring. A less-unsaturated five-membered-ring relative still scores 0.3542726928004173. Elsewhere, the cited fused cumulated-double-bond variant scores 0.18422963024144726 beside a conventional aryloxy/nitrile leader at 0.48839749189747395. The structural concern is tied to specific ring/bond relationships, rather than ring presence alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-size and bond-order changes do not consistently preserve credible geometry, and can concentrate output on small-ring cumulenes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring contraction, expansion, fusion and bond-order changes chemically coherent as joint local transformations. Maintain access to saturated or conventionally unsaturated alternatives that preserve the useful substituent arrangement. Let current-session observations determine which geometries and saturation states are useful, while keeping the consequences of small-ring cumulene formation distinguishable from ordinary ring edits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories identifies unspecified atom stereocentres in 351, 251, 451, 316 and 378 proposals in the brief task order, and assigned centres in none. The cited structures include substituted oxygen rings, chloroalkyl side chains, fused or bridged amines, acetal-like centres and a sulfinyl centre. Several simple aromatic or linear-linker leaders are achiral, so the gap concerns the structures that actually admit configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configurationally rich molecules are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configurations where chemically defined and preserve those specifications through local structural changes. Provide coherent configured alternatives around accepted arrangements and compare them through available feedback. The absence of specified configurations establishes missing representation, without identifying a universally favorable stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited zero-score examples include methane, hydroxylamine, acetylene, a long acyclic polyamine and a large repeated sulfur/amide assembly. A duplicated aromatic/amine-arm structure scores 0.046770493414912545 despite near-limit values for simpler arylpiperazine/linker members. Conversely, the compact 32-heavy-atom diazepinone-containing molecule scores 0.26493557493264663, above larger brominated biaryl relatives in its displayed family. The observations support context-dependent molecular scale.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing output can destroy a useful connected arrangement through extreme fragmentation or duplication of large motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore growth, contraction and linker changes that retain a coherent core and useful donor, acceptor, accessible-amine and aromatic relationships. Include alternatives between tiny fragments and multiplication of whole favorable arms, allowing accepted observations to determine useful size for the current objective without any hidden-task identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Different seeds produce aryloxy nitriles, N-acyl benzimidazoles, anilinoquinazolines, arylpiperazines, fused lactams and compact sulfur/nitrogen frameworks, yet the upper excerpts repeatedly decorate one neighborhood. Small local alternatives sometimes retain useful scores, while whole-fragment growth or electronic-context changes do not. The cited arylpiperazine/linker member scores 0.9999993790262016, whereas a piperazine with its nitrogens incorporated into amide and thiourea environments scores 0.00015556264858674598. These whole structures do not isolate a causal property, but they show why nitrogen count or a shared ring name is insufficient chemical coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variety is not accompanied by consistent coverage of useful core and functional-group arrangements within each leading chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted core families and explore core, linker and attachment alternatives that preserve useful functional-group placement and electronic context. Represent the distinctions among accessible saturated amines, amide nitrogens, heteroaromatic nitrogens and other polar environments when generating alternatives. Assess chemical variety through those relationships as well as the existence of a new molecular graph.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
